summary: Add durable mission-owned dedicated scratch with native final release and bounded dry-run orphan inventory

replay.detail: New scratch acquisitions revalidate their stable activity occurrence and immutable specification against host-local intent and receipt records. Replaying a released acquisition refuses resurrection. Existing missions without scratch declarations keep their current behavior.

schema.detail: Adds the host-local scratch_resources_v1 custody table and host/identity index without changing existing lane admission accounting. Intent, receipt, release tombstone and optional quarantine-handoff state persist independently of the allocation. Existing native execution identities gain optional PID and start-token evidence; missing legacy evidence remains unknown. Reinstalling an older binary does not remove these records.

rules.detail: Opted-in mission scratch gains native final-release work after authored finalizers and native consumer quiescence on success, failure and cancellation. Mission deadline expiry skips this work; inventory is read-only and no automatic orphan reclamation is enabled.

compatibility.detail: The new typed scratch and inventory operations require an execution host with this implementation. Older hosts do not support these resource operations. Mixed-version execution and downgrade with outstanding scratch custody have not been verified; keep custody-bearing runs on supporting hosts until release is confirmed.

downtime.detail: No additional service restart or coordinated outage is required by this opt-in adapter; restart-to-API and restart-to-health timings were not measured.

manual.detail: Choose an explicitly disposable private dedicated scratch root for new acquisitions. After a mission deadline or interrupted finalization, inspect resources scratch-inventory on the execution host. Unknown ownership or consumers are not authorization to remove a directory.

recovery.detail: Interrupted intent, creation, receipt and release resume through the original acquisition identity under the current host authority. Linux physical removal uses a private no-replace quarantine handoff and verifies the captured allocation before deletion; mismatch and interrupted creation retain custody. Current Linux process cwd observations, not historical ancestry, establish exclusion. Non-Linux physical retirement is unsupported and retains custody. Stale generations retain custody. Keep a supporting binary while unreleased records exist; the bounded orphan inventory never deletes allocations, and no fleet-wide recovery policy is enabled.
